pairs.subject: canvas-graph
pairs.evidence: features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:249 Hover is local state of the whole canvas component, so every hover change re-runs the node map and degreeOf over all edges for every node: an O(n·e) re-render of all nodes for one node's state change, against rung 3 'nodes re-render on their own changes only'.

techniques.evidence: features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:249 Nodes are not memoised and degree is recomputed on every hover or focus render.

features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:259 Single tab stop with roving focus, role=group (line 167) so the operable nodes are not collapsed, node labels carry position and degree, and GraphNodeList renders the same slice as a list twin.
features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:223 Focus-context rendering: edges of the traced neighbourhood draw at full strength and everything else recedes.
features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:62 No camera. The data-to-viewBox mapping is stated once (px/py), and there is no hand-written inverse because hit-testing is done by DOM elements.
features/dashboard/components/StateGraphCanvas.tsx:281 Selection is click and keyboard only. There is no drag, pan or marquee, so there is no click-vs-drag gesture to disambiguate.

pairs.subject: canvas-graph
pairs.evidence: features/dashboard/graphTraversal.ts:93 Arrow keys only pick among a node's graph neighbours, so there is no independent spatial axis (nearest node in screen direction), and a node with no edges cannot be reached by arrows at all; the technique asks for both spatial and topological navigation.

techniques.evidence: features/dashboard/graphTraversal.ts:93 Spatial direction and topology are merged into one arrow rule. There are no distinct topological shortcuts and no pure spatial navigation, and isolated nodes are only reachable via Home/End or the list twin.
features/dashboard/stateSlice.ts:206 The slice's generated slot layout reads input that is canonically ordered by durable identity (pspId, then IČO), so identical data gives an identical picture.

pairs.registryProposal: For a read-only renderer that already ships a list twin, the read-only paragraph says the twin may carry the whole keyboard contract, while 'Offer both axes' reads as unconditional. The technique should say whether partial in-canvas navigation (topology-only arrows) beside a complete twin counts as a deviation.
